events.summary: Nintendo and Sony both flagged the impact from surging memory prices on their games businesses on Friday, as the artificial intelligence boom constrains chip supply and deepens disruptions across the tech sector.  "Super Mario" maker Nintendo said that higher component costs, particularly memory, and the impact of tariffs is expected to add roughly 100 billion yen ($638 million) to costs in the current financial year.  "The very fact that Nintendo felt compelled to act (price increase) suggests the rise in memory costs has become severe enough that it could no longer be absorbed internally - and, crucially, that there is little prospect of those cost pressures easing in the near term," HSBC analyst Kazunori Ito said.
